newsitem.title: USA: Hewlett-Packard Q2 earnings below consensus.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett-Packard Q2 earnings below consensus.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Corp. said Thursday net earnings grew eight percent in its second fiscal quarter to April 30, falling short of Wall Street's consensus estimates as it cited disappointing order and revenue growth.
The company said a tough comparison with last year's strong second quarter, currency effects of a strong dollar and slowing in some markets constrained the company's growth rates.
The second-largest U.S.-based computer maker said U.S. orders fell by two percent during the quarter, while orders outside the United States rose by seven percent.

Net earnings for the quarter were $784 million, or $0.75 a share. This compares to analysts' mean estimates of $0.80 a share, according to First Call. Last year, net earnings were $723 million, or $0.69 a share, restated to reflect a two-for-one stock split completed in July 1996.
The results were released after the market close.
Hewlett-Packard shares were halted at the close, with the last trade up 2-1/4 at 58-7/8 just shy of the day's high of 59 and the all-time trading high of 60.
Hewlett-Packard Chairman, President and CEO Lewis Platt said the company managed to generate good profit margins despite the slowing order growth.
Cost of goods sold was 65.2 percent compared with 65.8 percent in the year-ago period, the company said.
"Our cost-of-sales result was excellent, and we continued to make progress in managing our operating assets and in generating cash," Platt said in a statement.
"We're disappointed, however, with order and revenue growth," he said. "A tough comparison with last year, as well as currency effects and slowing in some markets, affected our growth rates."
Net revenue for the quarter was $10.3 billion, up from $9.9 billion in last year's second quarter, when revenue had surged 33 percent from the prior year.

But net revenue in the United States was $4.4 billion, an increase of just 1 percent compared with the year-ago quarter, while net revenue from outside the United States rose 7 percent to $5.9 billion.

Orders for the quarter were $10.4 billion, a 3 percent rise from a year ago, when orders had jumped 24 percent from the year-earlier period. Without the effects of currency-exchange rates, the company's order growth this quarter would have been approximately 3 percentage points higher, HP said.
In the United States, orders declined by 2 percent to $4.6 billion, while orders from outside the United States rose 7 percent to $5.8 billion.
David Wu, an analyst at ABN AMRO Chicago Corp, noted the most marked weakness in order growth was in the United States, where "you can't blame the dollar for that."

Analysts said there were signs the printer market, which HP dominates, has slowed. The earnings disappointment could touch off selling in selected other technology issues Friday, but probably not to the extent that HP's profit warning of last July, which sent a chill through the sector.
"I think there's going to be collateral damage," one analyst said ahead of the company's conference call with the financial community at 5 p.m. EDT on Thursday afternoon.
